size.note: Newman's Birds gives about 60 cm. Wingspan: Wikipedia gives 1.50 m. Mass: Newman's Birds gives 1–1.8 kg.

habitat: East coastal regions with oil/raffia palms; in South Africa largely the KZN coast (Newman's). Rare visitor to Kruger.

distribution.note: Only 31 GBIF records in the park (far north 8, north 1, central 3, south 19; counted 13 November 2026), too few to say where it is recorded most.

summary: A distinctive white vulture-like raptor with black wings and tail; horn-coloured bill and legs (Newman's). Rare visitor and localised resident to the KZN coast; not a regular Kruger species.

similar.note: White-backed Vulture is larger, brownish, with a bare neck and white back patch — not clean white with black wings (Newman's).

research.note: Status is omitted. This is a rare visitor in Kruger, and the site has no vagrant status. The vocabulary is resident, intra-african-migrant, palearctic-migrant, and the older summer-migrant. No seasonal plumage change; immature brown. Gaps: Only 31 GBIF records in Kruger box — rare visitor. Images from Ndumo (KZN), not Kruger. Photos left out: A repeated file was omitted. Diet includes oil-palm fruits as well as carrion/crabs (BE/Wikipedia). monthsPresent set from Newman/SABAP seasonality cross-checked with GBIF Kruger month facets (not abundance). SABAP1 says breeding birds in northern KwaZulu-Natal are resident and vagrants wander widely, so status stays omitted for Kruger.
